openwrt_wiki.einleitung: TP-Link Archer C20 v1 is a router with a 5-port FE switch and non-detachable antennas, based on MediaTek MT7620A + MT7610E. As compared to the newer models, only v1 of the device comes with a USB port.
openwrt_wiki.installation_warnung: You need to use TFTP or DUMP to install. Do not flash from the stock UI because you will get an lzma kernel decompression error and you'll have to use serial console to recover from soft-brick. The reason why this router gets bricked so easily is because the bootloader (when doing a TFTP upload) always starts writing flash at address 0x0, overwriting the U-Boot partition as well in the process, thus serial console for recovery will not work and the only way to recover from this brick is by flashing the chip directly by SPI programmer. TFTP recovery method is fine when recovery firmware is official file since it contains boot partition, but OpenWrt does not.
openwrt_wiki.installation_tftp: uboot aus Stock-Firmware ausschneiden: dd if=Archer_C20v1_0.9.1_4.0_up_boot(160427)_2016-04-27_13.53.59.bin of=uboot.bin bs=512 count=256 skip=1; cat uboot.bin <openwrt-factory> > ArcherC20V1_tp_recovery.bin; PC 192.168.0.66/24, TFTP-Server; an LAN-Port anschliessen, WPS/Reset druecken und einschalten, 10 s halten; Flashen dauert bis 20-25 min; danach OpenWrt unter 192.168.1.1. Linux-Variante: WPS beim Start halten, nach 10 s holt der Router ArcherC20V1_tp_recovery.bin von 192.168.0.66, danach leuchtet eine weisse LED.
openwrt_wiki.back_to_stock: Immer gestrippte Firmware (ohne uboot) per OpenWrt flashen: dd if=Archer_C20v1_0.9.1_4.0_up_boot(160427)_2016-04-27_13.53.59.bin of=ArcherC20_v1_stripped.bin skip=257 bs=512. Note: Never attempt TFTP install method to flash this stripped firmware, otherwise router will hard brick.
openwrt_wiki.gehaeuse_oeffnen: Remove two screws under the devices, then pop the black top off (needs some force to get it off)
openwrt_wiki.serial: There should be 4 pads (J2) looking from the front on the right side, where the square pad is vcc 3.3V. Pinfolge: VCC GND Tx Rx. To make a successful connection, you'll have to solder 0 Ohm resistors on slots R600 and R601 as shown below. If you don't have those, then you can simply put a solder blob over them to complete circuit. Serial connection parameters: 115200, 8N1

openwrt_git_support.betreff: ramips: add support for TP-Link Archer C20 v1
openwrt_git_support.text: TP-Link Archer C20 v1 is a router with 5-port FE switch and non-detachable antennas. It's very similiar to TP-Link Archer C50. Also it's based on MediaTek MT7620A+MT7610EN.
openwrt_git_support.LED-Hinweis: WAN LED in this devices is a dual-color, dual-leads type which isn't (fully) supported by gpio-leds driver. For now, we support/use only the blue part of the LED.
openwrt_git_support.5GHz-Hinweis (2017): MT7610EN ac chip isn't not supported by LEDE. Therefore 5Ghz won't work.
openwrt_git_support.Factory image notes: version 3 of TP-Link header, without RSA signature (at least in case of devices sold in Europe); non-zero "Additional Hardware Version" required; vendor GUI accepts files but flashed image gets corrupted
openwrt_git_support.Flash instruction 1 (UART): PC 192.168.0.66/24 + tftp; beim Start Taste "4" fuer U-Boot-CLI; setenv serverip 192.168.0.66; tftp 0x80060000 <factory.bin>; erase tplink 0x20000 0x7a0000; cp.b 0x80060000 0x20000 0x7a0000; reset
openwrt_git_support.Flash instruction 2 (ohne UART): uboot.bin aus Original-Firmware (dd ... bs=512 count=256 skip=1) vor factory.bin haengen -> ArcherC20V1_tp_recovery.bin; PC 192.168.0.66/24; Reset-Taste druecken, einschalten, ca. 6-7 s halten bis Download beginnt

openwrt_git_factory_entfernt.betreff: ramips: remove factory image for TP-Link Archer C20 v1
openwrt_git_factory_entfernt.text: Similarly to the Archer C2 v1, the Archer C20 v1 will brick when one tries to flash an OpenWrt factory image through the TP-Link web UI. The wiki page contains an explicit warning about this. Disable the factory image altogether since it serves no purpose.
